name: horror
quote: I hit a baby deer with the car!
description: A strong sense of aversion to an event that is perceived as being likely to damage the body or an important social identity of you or a person important to you. Horror is fear with disgust.
perceptions: Something very unpleasant happened or is happening.
This event may cause damage and seems like it could contaminate your mind, a social identity, or your body.
results: desire to revert the event or contain the damage

guidance.description: If you're having trouble dealing with the memory of something horrible, consider seeking support or professional help.

variations.name: social horror
variations.description: If the experience is caused by someone breaking an important social rule, it may come with contempt. You may be worried about the implications of others not following this rule.
perceptions: Someone is breaking an important social rule.
You are unsettled that flauting the rule could contaminate the social environment.
You're worried about the implications of a contaminated environment to your selfself and other important people.
results: desire to put things back in order

variations.name: self horror
variations.description: If the experience is caused by the self breaking a social rule, it may come with guilt.
perceptions: You realize that you are unintentionally breaking a social rule.
You view the rule as important.

variations.name: suprised horror
variations.description: If the experience was completely unexpected, it may come with shock.
perceptions: Something very unpleasant happened or is happening.
results: desire to revert the event or contain the damage

comparisons.description: Horror is fear mixed with disgust or contempt.
People sometimes use the term 'horrified' to mean 'I have a strong aversion to this thing.' We like to inflate our experiences to make a point.

commentaries.quote: The basis of all true cosmic horror is violation of the order of nature, and the profoundest violations are always the least concrete and describable.
People who love horror films are people with boring lives... when a really scary movie is over, you're reassured to see that you're still alive and the world still exists as it did before.
